subject: Custody & Deployment Rights — proposed pathway for on-prem addendum
messages:
From: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@avalondx.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Boyd <claire.boyd@avalondx.com>, External Counsel <contracts@mcbee-llp.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — custody / escrow alternatives

Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As part of our procurement checklist we need clearer language on two items for the on-prem addendum and order form:

1) Deployment rights: confirmation that Avalon will be granted a perpetual runtime license for the model binaries we deploy on-prem (we understand weights remain under Redwood IP, but need a commercial runtime grant).
2) Custody / escrow-like access: procurement has asked whether we can provide an auditable custody path for model artifacts and KMS-wrapped keys in the event of Redwood insolvency or acquisition. They flagged escrow as their first preference but are open to alternatives (time-capsule S3 + key-handback protocol).

I'm attaching our preliminary redlines (Avalon_Redlines_v2.pdf). Can you put together the options Redwood can accept (preferred language + what we would need operationally)? We need something to present to our CFO and legal next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Shaw
Sr. Procurement Manager, Avalon Diagnostics
Attachments: Avalon_Redlines_v2.pdf

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@avalondx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — custody / escrow alternatives

Evan — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. High level response while we scope operational needs:

- Deployment rights: we can offer a time-limited exclusive runtime license for the binaries deployed in Avalon’s environment, with an option to renew or convert to a perpetual runtime license on defined commercial terms. We cannot assign IP for model weights, but can provide a nontransferable runtime sublicense scoped to Avalon’s production use.

- Custody/escrow: Redwood does not currently use third-party escrow services by default. We can offer two practical alternatives that legal & infra can support:
  a) Key-handback protocol + certified export bundle: in an insolvency trigger we will provide an encrypted bundle of model artifacts plus KMS-wrapped keys under an attestation process (requires both parties to complete key-exchange steps and an agreed escrow trigger).
  b) Third-party escrow (customer-funded): we will coordinate with your counsel on an approved escrow agent and provide a signed snapshot on a cadence (quarterly or at release milestones). This is operationally heavier but common for regulated customers.

I'll pull in Marcus (infra lead) and Rishi (legal ops) for specifics (what we can deliver, timelines, and sample contract language). If Avalon prefers the escrow agent route we can propose a shortlist.

Next steps: Marcus to confirm technical deliverables and time-to-produce export bundle; Rishi to draft two MSA addendum clauses (runtime grant + custody trigger) and propose warranty/repurchase language. I'll consolidate and send a one-pager for your CFO by Tue EOD.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@avalondx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — custody / escrow alternatives

Evan / team — quick tech note on feasibility: we can create an "export-ready" bundle that includes model graph, tokenizers, and a deterministic runtime shim. Operational constraints and timelines:

- Snapshot cadence: we can produce release snapshots on demand (requires 5 business days) or quarterly for automation.
- Keys: we will provide KMS-wrapped keys; for handback we need an out-of-band attestation (2-of-3 sigs) to protect both parties.
- Verification: we can include checksums and a signed manifest. Full reproducibility requires we ship the runtime shim and document deterministic seed/flags (we should mark this as a commercial deliverable due to engineering effort).

I'll attach a short options table (Custody_Options_Table.xlsx) with estimated lead times and one-time engineering cost buckets. If Avalon wants third-party escrow we will need contact for their counsel to agree SOC/controls baseline.

Cheers,
Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Custody_Options_Table.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@avalondx.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — custody / escrow alternatives

Evan / Claire / Priya — draft legal positions from Redwood (high level):

1) Runtime license clause (to add to Order Form/Addendum): grant to Customer a non-transferable, royalty-bearing runtime license to use the supplied runtime bundle on Customer-controlled infrastructure for the Term. Option to convert to perpetual runtime license upon payment of a pre-agreed fee within 90 days of contract signature.

2) Custody trigger & delivery: define a narrow insolvency trigger (e.g., appointment of receiver, filing for bankruptcy, failure to operate for X days despite remediation) that initiates delivery of an encrypted export bundle to Customer and to an optional mutually-agreed escrow agent. Redwood requires a certification step (legal letter + mutually-agreed custodian signature) before key release.

3) Limitations & warranties: Redwood will warrant that the export bundle corresponds to the shipped runtime; we will not warrant model accuracy or promise ongoing updates unless under a paid maintenance schedule. Any export or escrow interaction will carry fees to cover engineering and legal coordination.

4) Audit/Controls: Redwood can provide attestation of delivery and a signed manifest. For customers requiring SOC2-level escrow controls, we recommend third-party escrow and will coordinate but not certify the agent (customer to select & fund).

I'll circulate redline language after we confirm Avalon’s preferred trigger definition and whether they want a third-party escrow agent involved.

-Rishi
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Boyd <claire.boyd@avalondx.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@avalondx.com>, External Counsel <contracts@mcbee-llp.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — custody / escrow alternatives

Team — thanks for the swift turnaround and the options. A few clarifications from Avalon legal & procurement: 

- Avalon prefers the third-party escrow agent model for independence. Procurement will fund the escrow fees. Please propose a shortlist of 2–3 agents and the information Redwood would need to enable periodic snapshots.
- For the insolvency trigger, our counsel proposes a 30-day remediation window rather than an immediate delivery upon filing — that aligns with our internal risk committee. Is Redwood comfortable with the remediation window and the certification steps Rishi outlined?
- On runtime grant: we like the "option to convert to perpetual" approach but need clearer cost bands. Can Redwood provide a ballpark conversion fee range and whether it is pro-rated by months of service?

We have a procurement meeting on Wednesday; if Redwood can send the shortlist + one-pager (technical deliverables + legal bullets + estimated costs) by Tue EOD we can take it to the CFO.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Boyd
Head of Legal Ops, Avalon Diagnostics
Attachments: Procurement_SOW_Draft.docx
